intro: Music directors and composers make creative calls, coordinate performers and lead groups, skills used in art direction and media. The closest of the 25 careers below is Art Directors, with an 86% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $114,850, which is 56% more than the $73,710 music directors and composers earn.
why_it_works: Directing music means hearing what is wrong, explaining what you want and getting many people to perform as one. O*NET rates judgment at 3.5 out of 5 for this job, coordination at 3.38 and persuasion at 3.25. Art direction, writing and film editing use the same creative leadership. Almost every match needs no extra schooling. The gaps are reading people and managing time.
tips: Advertising and Promotions Managers earn $133,660, which is 81% more, and value creative direction.
Film and Video Editors earn $75,420, or 2% more, and use your sense of timing and pacing.
Public Relations Managers earn $146,910 and are a 68% match.

faq.q: What jobs can former music directors do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Art Directors (86%), poets, lyricists and creative writers (84%) and Writers and Authors (77%), based on O*NET 31.0. Film and Video Editors are 76% matched and earn $75,420, which is 2% more than the $73,710 median for music directors and composers.

faq.q: Which careers for music directors pay more?
faq.a: 17 of the 25 matches pay more. Marketing Managers earn $166,790 (126% more), Public Relations Managers $146,910 (99% more) and Advertising and Promotions Managers $133,660 (81% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. These roles value creative leadership.

faq.q: Do music directors need another degree?
faq.a: Usually not. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than music directors and composers already have, including 9 of the top 10, while 2 need a graduate degree. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 68% of workers in the closest match.

faq.q: What skills should music directors learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are social perceptiveness, time management, operations analysis and operations monitoring. Managing people already rates 3.12 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so business planning is the main step toward media and marketing leadership.
